rv.q: Antihero actor Garry becomes a magnificent new kind of beast as Gerri, played with blistering hilarity by Tracy-Ann Oberman
Ultimately, this remains an average Coward play receiving a competent rather than inspired production.
Overall, this is an excellent evening of entertainment, with a wonderful cast bringing Coward's sharply defined (but gender-switched) characters to life.

There is much to admire in Oberman’s bold reimagining of the classic play and her performance as Geri, but the situation never quite rings true and at times, it feels like we are watching a play within a play and that the director will step forward and say let’s do that scene again.
